title: Method for the estimation of institutional quality indexes using fuzzy logic
author: Ribeiro

steps.title: Prepare MATLAB environment
steps.instruction: Open MATLAB® R2018a and ensure the Fuzzy Logic Toolbox is installed and licensed.

steps.title: Create two fuzzy inference systems
steps.instruction: Instantiate two separate FIS objects (FIS 1 and FIS 2); each will contain six input variables and two output variables.

steps.title: Define variables and contexts
steps.instruction: Assign the six inputs of FIS 1 to the relational and economic context and the six inputs of FIS 2 to the social and local context; each FIS will produce two outputs, giving four institutional‑environment indexes in total.

steps.title: Assign membership functions
steps.instruction: For all input variables use triangular or singleton membership functions (triangular: parameters a ≤ m ≤ b; singleton: μ=1 at x=m, 0 elsewhere). For all output variables use strictly triangular membership functions.

steps.title: Map linguistic terms to fuzzy numbers
Construct rule bases
steps.instruction: Create a total of 85 IF‑THEN rules (38 for FIS 1, 47 for FIS 2). Break them down by context: Relational (18 rules = 3 × 3 × 2), Economic (20 = 5 × 2 × 2), Social (20 = 5 × 2 × 2), Local (27 = 3 × 3 × 3). Use the logical connective AND for antecedent aggregation; assign equal weight to every rule (no custom weighting).

steps.title: Select Mamdani inference method
steps.instruction: Configure each FIS to use the Mamdani (MIMO‑compatible) inference engine; choose the min operator for AND (intersection) and the max operator for OR (union).

steps.title: Run fuzzy inference
steps.instruction: For each observation (e.g., each tilapia‑farming unit), input the crisp values of the six indicators into the appropriate FIS, perform fuzzification, apply the rule base, aggregate rule outputs, and obtain the fuzzy output sets.

steps.title: Defuzzify using centroid
steps.instruction: Apply the Center‑of‑Area (CoA) defuzzification method to each fuzzy output set: CoA = ∑μA(xk)·xk / ∑μA(xk). This yields crisp index values ranging from 0 (worst) to 100 (best).

steps.title: Interpret institutional indexes
steps.instruction: Record the four crisp outputs (relational, economic, social, local) for each unit; values close to 100 indicate a highly favorable institutional environment, while values near 0 indicate a poor environment.
